title: Cisco Can Finally Sell Lots Of Supercomputers And Their Networks
gist: Cisco posted record Q4 F2026 revenue of $17.25 billion (up 17.6%) with AI orders driving growth, taking $9.3 billion in fiscal-2026 hyperscaler AI orders led by its Silicon One ASICs and Acacia-derived optical transceivers amid a scarcity of 400/800 Gb/sec optics. The author argues Cisco can sell large AI systems to neoclouds, sovereigns, and enterprises via UCS, but margins hinge on selling its own silicon and networking rather than reselling NVIDIA gear.

insights.claim: Cisco's Q4 fiscal-2026 revenue reached $17.25 billion, up 17.6 percent and the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with operating income up 23.9 percent to $4.26 billion and net income up 36.7 percent to $3.86 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Profits growing faster than revenue is the ideal mix and shows the AI networking boom is accretive at the top line for Cisco.
insights.quote: Cisco's overall revenues came in at $17.25 billion, up 17.6 percent and the highest quarterly revenues in the company's very long history.

insights.claim: Cisco ended the quarter with $15.92 billion in cash and $46.7 billion in revenue backlog, both of which have been roughly flat over the past two years but may grow with expected late-2026 and 2027 GenAI spending.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A large but flat backlog poised to grow signals the AI-driven demand wave is still ahead rather than fully booked.
insights.quote: The company ended the quarter with $15.92 billion in the cashbox and $46.7 billion in revenue backlog across its products.

insights.claim: For full fiscal 2026 Cisco had $63.33 billion in sales (up 11.8 percent) and net income of $13.27 billion (up 26.9 percent), and guides fiscal 2027 to $72.2-73.4 billion, up about 15 percent at the midpoint.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The 15% guided growth acceleration into FY2027 is the market's forward signal on Cisco's AI-driven trajectory.
insights.quote: Cisco expects for sales to be between $72.2 billion and $73.4 billion, and that is up 15 percent at the midpoint of $72.8 billion.

insights.claim: Cisco now drives more than half of its revenues from software and services, a goal it has held since 2016, with the services business having doubled over the coverage period.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A majority software/services mix stabilizes margins and reduces reliance on lower-margin hardware resale.
insights.quote: Cisco now drives more than half of its revenues from software and services, which has been a company goal since 2016

themes.theme: AI orders from hyperscalers and clouds

insights.claim: Cisco took in $9.3 billion in AI system and component orders from hyperscalers and big clouds across fiscal 2026, including roughly $4 billion in Q4 alone, up by a factor of 4.9X year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A near-5X jump in hyperscaler AI orders quantifies how central the GenAI buildout has become to Cisco's growth.
insights.quote: Cisco said it had $9.3 billion in orders from these tech titans in all of fiscal 2026

insights.claim: Of Q4 hyperscaler orders, over $1 billion was for optics and just under $3 billion for AI systems (switch ASICs, switches, servers, routers, and software), with the author estimating $1.04 billion in optical transceivers (up 4X) and $2.96 billion in AI systems components (up 5.4X).
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The split shows optics and merchant systems both scaling fast, clarifying where Cisco's AI revenue concentration lies.
insights.quote: The company said it had over $1 billion in orders from these customers for optics, which means just under $3 billion went to AI systems orders

insights.claim: Cisco took another $475 million in Q4 AI orders from neoclouds and sovereigns (up 4.9X), bringing total AI orders to $4.48 billion, up 4X year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The non-hyperscaler AI segment is growing faster than the hyperscaler business, diversifying Cisco's AI customer base.
insights.quote: Cisco took in another $475 million in orders from neoclouds, sovereigns for AI components and systems, up 4.9X compared to Q4 F2025.

insights.claim: The non-hyperscaler part of Cisco's AI business is growing faster than the hyperscaler business, but the author expects it will be many years before the two cross, if ever, given Cisco's large merchant networking business with the tech titans.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Hyperscalers will remain the dominant AI revenue channel, so their capex cycles stay the key thing to monitor for Cisco.
insights.quote: it will probably be many years before the numbers cross – if ever, considering how much merchant networking business Cisco will do with these tech titans.

insights.claim: Cisco's Silicon One merchant ASICs converge switching and routing into one architecture with variants for scale-up networking to share memory across GPUs and XPUs, which the author calls transformative for Cisco's datacenter business.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Owning merchant silicon is Cisco's route to higher-margin AI networking versus reselling third-party gear.
insights.quote: The company's move into the merchant silicon market with its Silicon One ASICs, which converge switching and routing down to a single architecture

insights.claim: Cisco has sold a cumulative 850,000 transceivers at 400 Gb/sec and 75,000 at 800 Gb/sec, with the 800 Gb/sec ramp just starting and 1.6 Tb/sec beginning to ramp in next-generation systems later this year into early next year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The transceiver install base and the 800 Gb/sec/1.6 Tb/sec ramp mark where the optics upgrade cycle and future revenue sit.
insights.quote: it had sold a cumulative 850,000 transceivers running at 400 Gb/sec, and another 75,000 running at 800 Gb/sec.

insights.claim: In Q4 F2026 Cisco shipped 100,000 transceivers at 400 Gb/sec and 35,000 at 800 Gb/sec, and the author models roughly $6 billion in cumulative 400 Gb/sec transceiver sales and $915 million at 800 Gb/sec since the Acacia deal closed in March 2021.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of Cisco's optics franchise and its acceleration, a direct beneficiary of the GenAI optics shortage.
insights.quote: Best I can figure, Cisco has peddled a little more than $6 billion in 400 Gb/sec transceivers and $915 million in 800 Gb/sec transceivers.

insights.claim: A dearth of 400 Gb/sec and 800 Gb/sec switching and optical transceivers due to the GenAI boom has become a scarcity Cisco is exploiting, since good transceivers at those speeds are hard to find.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The optics supply shortage is a durable tailwind that lets Cisco monetize its Acacia transceiver capability.
insights.quote: There is a dearth of 400 Gb/sec and 800 Gb/sec switching and optical transceivers out there thanks to the GenAI boom

insights.claim: The author does not expect Cisco to become an ODM-class AI cluster maker like Supermicro or Dell, but does expect it to sell large AI systems to neoclouds, sovereigns, and enterprises that already buy its UCS systems and switching infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Defines Cisco's realistic AI-systems TAM as its existing installed base rather than commodity cluster volume.
insights.quote: we do expect it to be able to sell a few large AI systems to neoclouds, sovereigns, and large enterprises who already buy its UCS systems and its datacenter and campus switching infrastructure.

insights.claim: The author estimates Cisco has in excess of 95,000 UCS customers worldwide who upgrade incrementally to make room for and add GenAI systems in their datacenters.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 95,000-strong installed base is the incremental upgrade engine that compounds Cisco's AI-driven revenue over time.
insights.quote: I strongly suspect that Cisco has in excess of 95,000 UCS customers worldwide

insights.claim: The author estimates Cisco's aggregate datacenter server, switch, and router business (with software) was $8.81 billion in Q4 F2026, up 28.3 percent, with operating income around $2.16 billion, up 25 percent.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Sizes the real systems business driving Cisco's AI growth and its profitability, since Cisco does not break out UCS separately.
insights.quote: the datacenter server, switch, and router businesses (including their software components) comprised $8.81 billion in sales in Q4 F2026, up 28.3 percent year on year.

insights.claim: Several Middle Eastern sovereign wealth funds building out their own AI capabilities have chosen Cisco as their platform provider, representing net new business.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Sovereign AI buildouts are a fresh demand pool expanding Cisco's addressable market beyond upgrade cycles.
insights.quote: as is the case with the several sovereign wealth funds in the Middle East that are building out their own AI capabilities and that have chosen Cisco as their platform provider.

themes.theme: Margin risk from reselling NVIDIA gear

insights.claim: Cisco cannot make much margin reselling NVIDIA components and designs but can do fine selling its own chips, systems, and software, making the profit mix dependent on its own silicon content.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Whether AI revenue is accretive to earnings hinges on Cisco selling Silicon One and its own networking rather than shuffling NVIDIA hardware.
insights.quote: Cisco cannot make much margin reselling Nvidia components and designs, but it can do fine selling its own chippery, systems, and software.

insights.claim: If fiscal 2027 growth is mostly reselling NVIDIA gear rather than selling Cisco's own scale-out and scale-up networking, profits could come under pressure and not grow as fast as revenues.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors should watch the silicon/systems mix, not just headline AI revenue, to judge Cisco's margin trajectory.
insights.quote: if it is just a lot of shuffling Nvidia gear and not selling a lot of its own scale out and scale up networking, profits could come under pressure and not grow as much as revenues.

insights.claim: The author expects MRC networking to take off on AI systems for the resiliency it yields, driving heavy spending on transceivers and cables because idle GPU/XPU clusters burning power are extremely expensive.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Fault-tolerant MRC networking is a future demand driver for Cisco's optics and cabling, tied to the high cost of cluster downtime.
insights.quote: companies will be spending a hell of a lot of money on transceivers and cables to make their AI clusters more fault tolerant

themes.theme: Cloud versus on-premises AI demand thesis

insights.claim: The author frames the future of AI infrastructure as neither fully cloud nor fully on-premises, arguing three different approaches to corporate computing will coexist as the technology and economics get sorted out.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A multi-venue deployment world favors vendors like Cisco that sell into cloud, colo, and enterprise datacenters alike.
insights.quote: the glass is neither half full nor half empty when it comes to cloud versus on premises, but rather we need three different glasses to pour three different stiff drinks.

insights.claim: GenAI technologies will trickle down and create massive need for supercomputing-style systems delivering sustained token throughput akin to mainframe-class OLTP and batch processing, with the shift from chatbots to agentic AI being profound and expensive.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Positions enterprise agentic AI as the next large, high-cost hardware wave that Cisco's supercomputing systems can serve.
insights.quote: the shift from chattybot farting around to true agentic AI is going to be profound, and the hardware and systems software to deliver it are going to be expensive.
